purpose: How unusual is the balance of signed ranks for five paired packing comparisons?
meaning: Keep each packing comparison paired, omit exact zero differences, rank the remaining absolute differences and average ranks at ties. Add ranks by sign, then compare the absolute signed score with every fair-sign assignment of those same ranks.

definition.setting: A workshop compares two packing methods on five paired tasks. Each constructed A time is 10 minutes; its B time adds the task’s difference. Choose the first four differences and drag the fifth difference d₅. Follow that task through its absolute difference, data rank and signed contribution before counting the null sign patterns.

conditions: Five constructed paired differences use independent fair signs conditional on the nonzero magnitudes. Omit exact zeros before assigning tied average ranks.
definition.domain_notes: The five times are constructed. The conditional null requires independent fair signs given the nonzero absolute paired differences; a symmetric zero-centered difference model supplies the usual justification. Exact zeros are omitted before ranking, using the Wilcoxon convention rather than Pratt ranking. Tied absolute differences receive their average rank. This implementation enumerates all 2^n sign assignments of the observed midranks, with an inclusive two-sided absolute-score tail; it does not use an untied rank table or a normal approximation. Its doubled-rank comparisons are exact integers. n is four when d₅=0 and otherwise five. At most five nonzero pairs cannot produce a two-sided p below 2/32=0.0625 in this family, so even all-positive signs cannot meet a 0.05 cutoff. This is neither a probability that the null is true nor a general before/after median claim. Moving a difference changes the teaching construction, not evidence from a completed study.

properties.claim: Keep each packing comparison paired, omit exact zero differences, rank the remaining absolute differences and average ranks at ties. Add ranks by sign, then compare the absolute signed score with every fair-sign assignment of those same ranks.
properties.conditions: Five constructed paired differences use independent fair signs conditional on the nonzero magnitudes. Omit exact zeros before assigning tied average ranks.
properties.derivation: Data ranks are ordinal positions, with a tied block assigned its average position. Under the conditional fair-sign null, all 2^n independent sign assignments are equally likely. Count each assignment whose absolute signed rank score is at least the observed absolute score. Average ranks are half-integers, so doubling every rank gives integer scores and exact tie comparisons. The test uses magnitude order as well as sign; the simpler sign test uses signs alone.
